title: Structure of the human P2X3 receptor reveals the basis for subtype-selective inhibition by sivopixant
experiments_summary: 1. Protein expression and purification: Human P2X3 receptor was expressed in Sf9 insect cells using a baculovirus system with an N-terminal Twin-Strep/EGFP tag, solubilized in DDM detergent, purified via Streptactin affinity chromatography, TEV protease cleavage, and size-exclusion chromatography. 2. Cryo-EM structure determination: Purified hP2X3 receptor was mixed with 0.1 mM sivopixant, applied to Au R1.2/1.3 holey carbon grids, vitrified using a Vitrobot, and imaged on a Titan Krios at 300 kV with a Falcon 4i camera (7,464 movies collected). Data processing in CryoSPARC included motion correction, CTF estimation, template-based particle picking, 2D classification, ab initio reconstruction with C3 symmetry, 3D variability analysis yielding two distinct classes, heterogeneous refinement, nonuniform refinement, and local refinement, resulting in two maps: one at 2.95 Å (ATP-bound, 71,855 particles) and one at 3.34 Å (sivopixant+ATP-bound, 46,550 particles). Atomic models were built in Coot using existing apo (PDB: 5SVJ) and desensitized (PDB: 5SVL) structures as references and refined with PHENIX real-space refinement. 3. Structure-based mutagenesis and electrophysiology: Point mutations in hP2X3 (M75A, M75W, T82I, P84A, Q85A, M96A, M96W, M165A, M165W, F282A, F282W, Y285W, L298F) were introduced by site-directed mutagenesis into HEK293 cells. Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings (conventional or perforated patch using nystatin) were performed using an Axopatch 200B amplifier at −60 mV holding potential. ATP-dependent currents were recorded with perfusion of 1 µM or 0.3 µM sivopixant to assess sensitivity changes relative to wild type. 4. Gain-of-function (GOF) mutant design and testing: GOF mutants of hP2X1 (F92T/D97T/F106M/L179M/H296Y) and hP2X2 (E97D/K100T/E103Q/G105T/V114M/G189M) were constructed to introduce hP2X3-equivalent residues at five key positions. These mutants were expressed in HEK293 cells and tested by patch-clamp for sensitivity to sivopixant (1 µM) and camlipixant (0.1 µM and 10 µM). 5. ATP concentration-dependence recordings: Whole-cell patch-clamp experiments were performed on hP2X3-expressing HEK293 cells at varying ATP concentrations in the presence or absence of sivopixant to assess whether sivopixant inhibition was ATP-competitive. 6. AlphaFold3-based structural modeling: Predicted structural models of human P2X2/P2X3 heteromers in two stoichiometries (2:1 and 1:2) were generated using AlphaFold3. Sivopixant binding prediction was also attempted with Boltz-2, including runs with and without restraints on the five key residues. 7. Structural comparisons: The sivopixant+ATP-bound hP2X3 structure was superposed with structures of hP2X1, hP2X2, hP2X4, hP2X7, and the AlphaFold3-modeled P2X2/P2X3 heteromer, and with camlipixant-bound dog P2X3, BAY-1797-bound P2X4, and JNJ-54175446-bound P2X7 structures, to identify divergent residues at the portal of the central pocket (PCP). 8. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations: Four systems were simulated—hP2X3 with sivopixant+ATP, sivopixant alone, ATP alone, and apo—each embedded in a POPC lipid bilayer with SPC water and 150 mM NaCl. Systems were equilibrated using the DESMOND relaxation protocol and then simulated for ~0.5 µs each using the OPLS 2005 force field. Cα distances between Glu289 residues from adjacent subunits were monitored across trajectories to assess upper body domain dynamics as a function of sivopixant binding.
